title: Tissue clearing and three-dimensional imaging of the whole cochlea and vestibular system from multiple large-animal models
protocol: Dissect the porcine inner ear out of the skull.
Trim the dissected inner ear for tissue clearing.
Cut a rectangular window on top of the skull using a bone stryker.
Remove the brain and brain stem from the skull.
Locate the inner ears on the lateral sides of the skull.
Identify the superior margin of the petrous part.
Cut in parallel to detach the inner ear from the skull.
Flip the sample to reveal the tympanic membrane.
Trim the spongious mastoid bone using bone-cutting forceps.
Expose the apex of the cochlea.
Remove the stapes.
Remove the round window membrane.
Observe the dissected and trimmed inner ear top view and side view.
Cut a rectangular window through the bone on top of the skull using a bone stryker.
Remove the brain and brain stem.
Locate the inner ears on the lateral sides of the skull.
Cut right above the inner ear where the superior margin of the petrous part is located.
Cut the base of the skull in half using the bone stryker.
Detach the rest of the inner ear periphery from the skull.
Push the base of the skull back and separate the lateral parts including the inner ears from the rest of the skull.
Trim the excess bone around the inner ear using a bone stryker to remove temporal bone while keeping the cochlea intact.
Locate the tympanic membrane or middle ear.
Carefully trim the specimen without damaging the inner ear using bone-cutting forceps.
Trim the excess bones and make cuts in the spongious mastoid bone using bone-cutting forceps until the apex of the cochlea is found.
Remove the loose bone pieces, tissues, and ligaments using a scissor.
Use the bone nipper to trim any remaining temporal bone near the inner ear.
Remove the stapes and the round window membrane using a sharp (style 5) tweezer.
Transfer the inner ear into fixative solution I in a 50 mL tube.
Incubate the inner ear in the fixative solution at 25°C for 1–2 hours.
Fix the inner ear in fixative solution II for 12–20 hours at 4°C.
Wash the sample three times in 1× PBS for one hour each.
Decalcify the bone using decalcification buffer for 2–10 days based on the age of the animal, changing the buffer every 24 hours at 37°C on a shaker.
Separate the inner ear from the temporal bone if there is any remaining bone.

Dehydrate the sample using methanol gradients at 25°C on a shaker: Incubate in 20% methanol for two hours. Incubate in 40% methanol for two hours. Incubate in 60% methanol for two hours. Incubate in 80% methanol for two hours. Incubate in 100% methanol for two hours, repeating this step twice.
Decolorize the sample using decolorization buffer at 4°C for 12–20 hours on a shaker.
Rehydrate the sample using methanol gradients at room temperature on a shaker: Incubate in 100% methanol for two hours. Incubate in 80% methanol for two hours. Incubate in 60% methanol for two hours.
Incubate in 40% methanol for 2 hours.
Incubate in 20% methanol for 2 hours.
Incubate in PBS for 2 hours.
Immunolabel the samples.
Place the sample in a 50 ml tube and fill it with permeabilization solution.
Shake gently for 12–20 hours at 37°C.
Discard the permeabilization solution and replace with blocking buffer.
Shake for 12–20 hours at 37°C.
Immunolabel the sample with primary antibodies added to antibody buffer in a ratio of Vantibody:Vbuffer = 1:200.
Place the labeled sample at 37°C on a shaker for 5–7 days.
For smaller samples and younger animals, use 5 days.
Pick the tube size based on the sample size and minimize the solution volume to save immunolabeling reagents.
Wash the sample with washing buffer at 37°C on a shaker for 24 hours, changing the buffer every 6 hours.
If exchanging the washing buffer every 6 hours is not feasible, repeat four times with a minimum of 6 hours each.
Immunolabel the sample with secondary antibodies in antibody buffer (Vantibody: Vbuffer = 1:250) at 37°C on the shaker for 4–5 days.
Wash the sample with washing buffer at 37°C on a shaker for 48 hours.
Change the washing buffer every 6 hours if feasible.
Repeat the wash step eight times, ensuring each cycle is at least 6 hours long if frequent buffer changes are not possible.
Dehydrate the sample using methanol gradients in a 50 mL tube at 25°C on a shaker.
Incubate in 20% methanol for 2 hours.
Incubate in 40% methanol for 2 hours.
Incubate in 60% methanol for 2 hours.
Incubate in 80% methanol for 2 hours.
Incubate in 100% methanol for 2 hours, repeating this step twice (2×).
Delipidate the sample at 25°C on a shaker.
Incubate in delipidating solution I for 2 hours, repeating this step twice (2×).
Incubate in delipidating solution II for 0.5 hours four times (4×).
RI-match the sample at 25°C on a shaker.
Incubate in RI matching solution in a 50 mL tube at 25°C for 24 hours.
Repeat the incubation process three times (3×).
Minimize the air gap on top of the DBE to prevent oxidation and formation of peroxides.
Handle the sample very gently to avoid introducing bubbles inside the sample.
Optional: Build a perfusion chamber by drilling two holes in a 5 mL Eppendorf tube matching the microfluidics tube diameter.
Insert inlet and outlet microfluidic tubes through the drilled holes into the antibody buffer solution.
Run the pump to fill the microfluidic tubes with the antibody buffer, ensuring no bubbles form inside the tubes.
Place the sample within the chamber, making sure the solution covers the sample.
Position the inner ear so the round window can be accessed.
Connect an intrathecal catheter to the tubing inlet and run the pump to fill the catheter with the antibody buffer.
Gently insert the catheter into the round window.
Slowly close the tube cap.
Ensure the perfused solution exits from the oval window into a 5 ml reservoir at 37°C inside the incubator.
Make sure the outlet tube is submerged in the solution.
Cover the cap, holes, and tubes with parafilm.
Flow the solution using the perfusion pump at a rate of 1.9 μL/min.
Store the sample in PBS (RT) for short-term storage (one to two weeks).
For long-term storage, store samples in PBS/0.1% sodium azide at 4°C.
Ensure stored samples are kept in a dark space.
Imaging Timing: ∼10 h (for step 4)
Timing: ∼3 days (for step 5)
Mount the sample inside the imaging chamber.
Position the needle away from the region of interest to avoid blocking the illumination beam.
Mount the sample in an orientation that minimizes the distance light travels through the decalcified bone.
Ensure the desired region of interest lies in the XY plane for optimal resolution.
Use a sharp 30 ga needle when mounting the sample in DBE to prevent bubble formation.
Choose top-view or side-view mounting positions based on the specific sample (e.g., cochlea).
Embed the sample in a 0.8% agarose block if an alternative mounting technique is preferred, after tissue clearing and before imaging steps.
Mount samples via a needle for convenience.
Fill the chamber with DBE imaging solution; ensure it completely covers the detection objective lens and sample.
Create a small hole in the silicone membrane and stretch it over the objective tightly where the hole is in front of the lens.
Remove the imaging solution from the chamber as soon as imaging is completed.
Leave the sample in the immersion chamber for 30 min before imaging.
Observe if the sample orientation is optimal in the microscope field of view and make adjustments if needed.
Start imaging.
Set the pixel size to 0.65 × 0.65 μm².
Adjust the sampling along the axial direction (z) to 5, 10, or 15 μm based on the biological application.
Use 560 nm and 640 nm lasers to excite different fluorescence channels in the samples.
Use a 488 nm laser for autofluorescence to provide structural information.
For custom-built light-sheet microscopes, use Galvo X and Y mirrors to move the detection objective relative to the light-sheet position while imaging.
Construct an imaging chamber using iSpacer.
Stick the iSpacer on a glass slide.
Seal the glass slide and the iSpacer with silicon glue.
Let it dry for 30 minutes.
Select an iSpacer that is just slightly thicker than the sample height.
Mount the sample inside the iSpacer.
Fill the iSpacer with DBE.
Ensure the area of interest within the tissue faces the objective lens.
Glue the sample to adjust orientation if necessary, ensuring glue is dried before adding imaging solution.
Add imaging solution to fill the iSpacer completely, forming a slight convex surface.
Remove sticker from top of iSpacer and place a thin cover glass gently on top.
Clean residue of DBE using nail enamel to seal cover glass/iSpacer interface.
Let sealed cover glass/iSpacer dry for 5–10 minutes.
Mount the slide on the confocal stage.
Start imaging.
Change the confocal stage if needed to accommodate larger samples.
Use fresh DBE and a new iSpacer to remount the tissue.
Minimize the imaging volume to the area of interest initially.
